<a id="overview"></a>

# Overview

CLABOK is a command-line authoring tool for structured Markdown books. It keeps a book's structure, bodies and generated content in one deterministic store and renders the result as a README or as chapter files.

The problem it solves is documentation drift. When chapters, order, navigation and prose all live in text, every reorder becomes a manual edit and every link is a guess. CLABOK makes the structure data, so navigation, the index, anchors and numbering are generated from it.

The model is deliberately small. A book is a tree of chapters and subchapters, and each body is a block. A paragraph, a code sample and a note are blocks, so each one has an identifier, a lock scope and a rollback path.

The store is the single source of truth. A book is either open, extracted for editing, or closed and packed into one container. Rendered documentation is output; it is never read back as input.

The tool owns the error-prone parts: numbering, anchors, navigation, the document index and generated content such as badges and the repository tree. Authors write Markdown bodies and assign structure; the tool derives the rest.

The CLI is the complete interface. Automation, agents and CI use it. The terminal UI is an optional view over the same core services and is never a second implementation of book behavior.

What CLABOK is not: it is not a static site generator, a visual editor, a database or a web service. The only server it can start is the separate grammar server.

The guide is ordered from concepts to practice. The next chapter explains the book model, then installation and the first book follow, then the authoring features, output, configuration, the command reference, the terminal UI and the project itself.
